Subject: Regional binding commitment / transient egress question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. HelixCare is moving towards locking down EU-only residency for patient-identifiable prompts and embeddings. Before we proceed with a purchase order we need clarity on two items so our legal and security teams can sign the DPA:

1) Can Redwood commit to EU anchoring for production traffic (not dev/test) such that data is processed in EU-region hosts by default?

2) We understand there are failure and capacity events. What is your maximum permitted transient cross-region processing window (in hours) for EU-bound requests when failover or burst routing is required? We need this reflected in the DPA (upper bound and notification SLA).

3) For any transient cross-region processing, what telemetry and evidence can you provide (aggregate audit logs, timestamps, KMS key location, and a post-incident report)?

I'm attaching our internal DPA request form (DPA_Request_Form.pdf).

Can you please confirm and, if needed, propose wording we can put into our legal team? Also include any addendum/DocuSign link for a temporary egress clause if you have one.

Best,
Lena
Head of Privacy Ops
HelixCare Health

Hi Lena,

Thanks for the clear list — appreciate the DPA form. Short answers up front:
- Yes, we can operate a customer-configured EU anchoring profile for production workloads so traffic is routed to EU-only placement by default.
- We can permit a temporary cross-region processing window for emergencies or capacity-driven bursts; the standard upper bound we propose is 48 hours, with a customer notification within 4 hours of the event and a follow-up post-incident report within 72 hours.
- Evidence: we provide time-stamped audit logs, routing decision traces, and key-location metadata (KMS region) for each incident. We can also produce a redacted post-incident report to include root cause and mitigations.

Options we suggest for contract language:
1) EU Anchoring: "Redwood will route and process Customer production requests in the EU region under normal operating conditions, subject to the exceptions below."
2) Temporary Egress Exception: "In the event of a capacity, availability, or security incident, Redwood may route EU-bound requests to an alternate region for a maximum period of forty-eight (48) hours. Redwood will provide Customer notification within four (4) hours of any such routing and will deliver a post-incident report within seventy-two (72) hours. Temporary routing will be limited to processing necessary to restore service and will not be used for batch reprocessing of historical customer data unless explicitly authorized by Customer."

Next steps:
- Looping in legal for precise DPA wording (cc'd: Jordan, Karthik).
- Can you share the HelixCare list of sensitive endpoints/data classes to scope the anchoring?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team,

Quick legal note to align on contract wording and a couple of conditions HelixCare will likely ask for:

1) We can accept the 48-hour cap as an upper bound, but we should include language that allows one pre-authorized extension of up to an additional 24 hours if both parties agree (we propose signed addendum via DocuSign).

2) Notification: we commit to an initial email and PagerDuty alert to the named contacts within four (4) hours. The DPA should include the minimum contents of that notification (time window, affected services, and KMS key region).

3) Evidence: we will provide a post-incident packet containing routing traces (CSV), audit-log excerpts (redacted PII), and KMS metadata. For extremely sensitive customers we can offer an option to escrow keys (customer-managed keys) for additional assurance — that would require a separate onboarding timeline.

Suggested DPA clause (single sentence for the DPA, details in an annex):
"Redwood will operate Customer production services in the EU region. In limited circumstances (capacity, operational stability, or security incidents), Redwood may route processing to alternate regions for no more than forty-eight (48) hours without prior Customer approval; any extension requires explicit written consent. Redwood will notify Customer within four (4) hours and provide a post-incident evidence package within seventy-two (72) hours. See Annex A for evidence and notification format."

Action items: Jordan to draft Annex A (evidence package schema), Karthik to confirm operational telemetry retention windows and anonymization process. I will draft the DocuSign addendum template.

-Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
